Linux, Intel macOS and isolated native Windows checks pass; those checks do not close the failed confinement requirements.

results.behavior: On private roots, restricted=true tokens denied FILE_WRITE_DATA, FILE_WRITE_ATTRIBUTES and WRITE_DAC but allowed DELETE and FILE_DELETE_CHILD. DeleteFileW, ordinary/POSIX file dispositions, Rust remove_file and PowerShell Remove-Item deleted files under read-only and outside a workspace-write grant. Workspace-write also moved an outside file into the workspace. The diagnostic exits 0 when its observations match disk; that is failed confinement evidence, not a passing sandbox. Raw machine SIDs remain in ignored logs.

33 unit and 19 enforcement cases pass. Both normal provider constructors refuse both confined modes on Windows. An explicit qualification chain tests the prototype: denied data writes, junctions, documented hard-link aliases, standing grants, failed spawn, bounded descendant cleanup, and simultaneous per-command temp write isolation. A second command can still delete another command's temp files; the deletion counterexample remains. Four independent enforcement processes pass 76 cases with no surviving scope process or fixture residue.

The built bake-rs hidden helper denies a read-only write and an outside workspace-write write, permits an inside write, and removes its private temp directory. The default product provider never selects the unqualified helper. These three observations do not prove deletion confinement.

The first full Windows workspace test run failed six existing skill-discovery cases because TEMP under the user home exposed real ancestor .agents/skills. Counts include targets completed before Cargo stopped: 636 passed, 6 failed, 1 ignored. Product code and assertions were not changed to hide the failure.

With a private TEMP/TMP outside the user home, Windows passes 1196 Cargo tests, 1 ignored, then workspace Clippy -D warnings and build. Linux full preflight passes 33 gates with 1 runtime-suite skip (no TypeScript runtime source changed); its Rust gate passes 1295 tests and 1 ignored, plus 22 native PTY cases and keyless eval smokes. Intel macOS passes 3 native gates: 1269 Cargo tests and 1 ignored, 20 PTY cases with 2 Linux-/proc skips, and keyless eval smokes. Command counts for preflight describe gates. Final production code equals the Mac snapshot; only a comment and Windows-only test cleanup changed afterwards, checked locally and on Windows.

negativeControls.missing: No deliberate implementation mutation was run in this slice. The Windows suite includes real unconfined write/orphan controls and the retained-token deletion counterexample, but they do not provide the complete fault-injection matrix.

missingEvidence.what: Windows deletion and source-side rename confinement
missingEvidence.reason: The retained restricted-token mechanism fails these requirements. A stronger mechanism must be chosen and qualified; this record does not accept weaker guarantees or close scope 04.

No deterministic kill at every create/assign/resume boundary or injected Win32 failure at every cleanup boundary. A killed runner triggers Job termination, but caller-level cancellation quiescence is not fully qualified.
Only one Windows x86_64 host, Linux x86_64 WSL2 and an Intel macOS host were used. No arm64 or minimum-OS qualification.

missingEvidence.reason: No live model run was made. The default Windows refusal detail now explains the deletion gap; a PR must handle the model-visible diagnostic under the eval rule. The current native evaluator runs POSIX with danger-full-access and cannot qualify Windows confinement.

rollback.observed: Test processes and private fixtures were cleaned up after the concurrent Windows run. The product default remains fail-closed on Windows. No release install, update or rollback was attempted.
